players.product: Enhanced geothermal (EGS) 24/7 baseload power from modular GeoBlocks (Cape Station geocluster, Utah) under long-term PPAs with hyperscalers, utilities and industrial buyers, grid-connected and behind-the-meter

quarterly_data.signal: Fervo's 10-Q key performance indicators as of June 30, 2026: ending active rig count 3; geothermal development portfolio of 3 MW Mature - Operating, 500 MW Mature - Under Construction, 550 MW Mature - Ready to Build, 3,000 MW Pipeline - Advanced Development and 48,550 MW Pipeline - Early Development, with a total geothermal lease position of 650,000 net acres. It expects its first GeoBlocks to be operational at the end of 2026, approximately 100 MW of operating capacity by early 2027 and 500 megawatts of cumulative operating capacity by the end of 2028. Of the approximately $7.2 billion contracted backlog, PPAs with several utilities represent approximately $5.7 billion. As of the filing date, 79 out of 80 governmental permits needed to commence commercial operations at Cape Station Phase I and 82 out of 179 for Phase II had been received.
quarterly_data.figure: 500 MW under construction; 550 MW ready to build; 3,000 MW advanced development; 48,550 MW early development; 500 MW cumulative operating capacity by end of 2028; utility PPAs ~$5.7 billion of ~$7.2 billion backlog

quarterly_data.signal: Fervo's 10-Q capital outlook (now on a calendar-year basis): total capital expenditures for the year ending December 31, 2026 are projected at approximately $1.3 billion ($399.3 million incurred in the six months ended June 30, 2026), consistent with the previously disclosed approximately $2.2 billion of cumulative capital expenditures for Cape Station Phase II through 2028. Its estimate of capital expenditures to construct a single 50-megawatt GeoBlock was approximately $7,000/kW as of June 30, 2026, inclusive of wellfield, surface facilities and plant equipment. Total supplier contractual commitments for materials and services were $488.3 million as of June 30, 2026, the majority relating to Cape Station Phase I and Phase II.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex ~$1.3 billion; Cape Phase II ~$2.2 billion through 2028; ~$7,000/kW per GeoBlock; supplier commitments $488.3 million

connects_to.relationship: enhanced geothermal power offtake (Geothermal Framework Agreement and power purchase agreements)

contracts.signal: Fervo's 10-Q describes the Geothermal Framework Agreement (GFA) with Google Energy LLC: Fervo committed to propose geothermal development projects representing at least one gigawatt to Google within two years and up to three gigawatts over the term. It is a binding framework but does not obligate Google to accept any project, sign a PPA or provide project financing; pricing is cost-plus targeted return subject to caps, floors and escalating discounts on expansion projects; Google has audit rights, rights of first refusal over portions of Fervo's pipeline and pays termination fees if it withdraws at certain development stages; either party may terminate if no definitive offtake agreement is executed by March 19, 2028.
contracts.units: at least one gigawatt proposed within two years; up to three gigawatts over the term

players.product: NovaLT and Frame 5 gas turbines plus Brush generators for behind-the-meter data-center power (Chart Industries thermal management added July 2026)

connects_to.relationship: Organic Rankine Cycle turbines and associated equipment for Fervo geothermal projects

contracts.signal: Fervo's 10-Q: critical components such as geothermal turbines, heat exchangers and control systems are primarily sourced from third-party suppliers like Turboden, Baker Hughes and other specialized manufacturers; certain specialized scopes such as the ORC turbines and associated equipment for specific projects are currently sourced primarily from Turboden and Baker Hughes under project-specific equipment contracts with multi-year delivery schedules (no broad framework supply agreements). Fervo has placed orders for critical components of Phase II of Cape Station.
